title: Company risk lattice and allhands decision games v0-1
content:
Purpose:
This doc frames a compact, playable set of scenarios (decision games) to bring the company together at the next all‑staff about tradeoffs across OKRs, risk tolerances, and resource reallocation. Goal is to surface boundary decisions for execs and leave the meeting with 3 concrete asks (owner + timeline).

Background/context (short):
- Q2→Q3 we expect resource pressure on Dedicated capacity rollout and Private onboarding.
- Several teams flagged: latency SLO slippage for long-sequence workloads; a potential spike in enterprise demand that could double Dedicated commit needs; and an unresolved proposal to accelerate Redwood Optimize heuristic into beta.
- Current OKR draft (linked above) has multiple competing stretch objectives tied to headcount and infra spend. Need a simple decision lattice to operationalize tradeoffs.

What is a "risk lattice" here (rough primer):
- Lightweight matrix mapping: Impact (customer/API reliability, revenue, technical debt) vs Probability (low/med/high).
- Each cell ties to a short set of actions and owners (e.g., "High impact / medium probability -> pre-approve 2-week budget to ramp Dedicated capacity + monitor 72h").
- We will use it to seed 3 break-glass simulation exercises in the all‑staff.

Simulation scenarios (3 short games):
1) "Burst of enterprise capacity" (15 mins):
   - Trigger: 2 customers sign Dedicated contracts, immediate 2x expected throughput.
   - Decision points: throttle new onboards vs accelerate autoscale? move committed GPU to burst pool? prioritize enterprise routes?
   - Risk lattice outcomes to consider: revenue upside vs latency SLO erosion for hosted API.
   - Expected ask: Execs pre-authorize a short-term burst budget (owner: VP Sales + Dir Platform).

2) "Quality regression on a model family" (15 mins):
   - Trigger: Eval harness flags 6% degradation on LLM-v2 config for safety/regressions after quantization change.
   - Decision points: rollback quantization profile for served versions? increase eval cadence and pause rollout? open canary to 10% traffic?
   - Risk lattice outcomes: customer trust/reliability vs cost of serving larger model.
   - Expected ask: Temporary freeze on rollout + add one SRE and one ML engineer to rollback/patch runbook (owner: Head of Applied ML).

3) "Latency tail on long sequences" (20 mins):
   - Trigger: production traces show 95th percentile latency for >2k token requests at 3x SLO.
   - Decision points: implement caching prefix-KV for affected routes; denylist long queries; push a lightweight model variant with optimized kernels?
   - Risk lattice outcomes: customer experience vs unit-cost tradeoff vs ops complexity.
   - Expected ask: deploy quick cache toggle and create an A/B rollout plan (owner: Serving Runtime lead + SRE).

All‑staff run-of-show (60–75 mins):
- 0–5m: Exec framing (CEO) — why we need collective decisions not just updates.
- 5–10m: Quick primer on risk lattice format (host: product-ops).
- 10–40m: Run scenarios 1 & 2 back-to-back as 15m micro-games (breakouts for 5m each).
- 40–60m: Scenario 3 (full 20m) + group synthesis.
- 60–70m: Exec panel rapid Q&A.
- 70–75m: Summarize 3 asks, owners, and next steps + calendar invites for decision trackers.

Facilitation notes / props: (notes to self)
- Prep 3 one‑slide scenario briefs with expected metrics and the risk lattice cell highlighted.
- Breakouts should have a template: 1) immediate decision, 2) secondary mitigation, 3) info needed for final decision, 4) recommendation.
- Use Miro board with lanes pre-created: "Revenue", "Reliability", "Cost", "Speed to ship".
- We must not run long by more than 5m; exec panel should be on standby for quick alignment.

Decision ladder and escalation (quick sketch):
- Level 1: Team-level mitigations (can be executed within 48–72h). Owner: Eng lead / PM.
- Level 2: Cross-team day-of decisions (require exec sign-off for budget/time reallocation < 2 weeks). Owner: Functional lead + Exec sponsor.
- Level 3: Strategic trade (changes to OKRs, material reallocation of committed capacity or hiring). Owner: CEO + CFO + CTO.

Measurement / artifacts we will produce post-all‑hands: (compact list)
- Decision tracker (spreadsheet) with: decision, owner, due date, acceptance criteria (1 pager).
- Short exec note summarizing outcomes and any OKR modifications.
- Follow-up mini-retrospective (2 weeks after) to record what stuck and what didn't.

Open questions / risks before we run: 
- Does finance want to pre-approve a small emergency budget for burst scenarios? (ping: CFO).
- Which OKRs are flexible vs committed for exec-level reallocation? Need a canonical list from product-ops.
- We must avoid turning this into a "blame session"; framing matters.

Next steps (immediate):
- [Aisha] Draft 3 slide briefs + risk lattice visuals by Feb 18.
- [Marco] Build Miro template + breakout prompts by Feb 18.
- [Sofia] Lock exec panel and confirm 15m CEO framing slot by Feb 17.
- [Ben] Create decision tracker spreadsheet and pre-populate with known risks by Feb 19.

Notes to self / rough language for invite: 
"All-staff: participatory decision simulation on tradeoffs, not a status dump. Bring pragmatic options, not just open problems. We'll finish with 3 clear asks and owners."

Appendix (short links & refs):
- Current OKR draft (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinternal/pages/OKR-2026-Q2-draft
- Eval harness failing run: JIRA-ML-901
- Support thread about long-sequence latency: #sre-longseq-traces (Slack)

----
Informal scratch notes (do not include in external comms):
- Keep slides light — execs want clear ask bullets.
- If scenario 1 edges toward revenue >2x, we might need a fast legal review for new contracts — add legal on call.
- Potential endorsement from sales leadership will materially change outcomes; loop them in early.

End.
